purpose: This medication is used to treat Parkinson's disease and similar conditions that cause problems with movement, stiffness, and tremors (shaking). It helps reduce symptoms like slow movement, muscle stiffness, and trembling. It can greatly improve your ability to move and do everyday activities.
how_it_works: Your brain uses a chemical called dopamine to help control smooth, coordinated movement. In Parkinson's disease, the brain does not make enough dopamine. Levodopa travels to your brain and gets converted into dopamine, helping replace what is missing. Carbidopa is added to help more levodopa reach the brain and reduce side effects like nausea.
common_side_effects: Nausea or upset stomach, especially when first starting the medicine. Dizziness or lightheadedness, particularly when standing up quickly. You may notice your urine, sweat, or saliva turning a darker or reddish color — this is harmless. Some people experience unusual movements (called dyskinesias), drowsiness, or vivid dreams.
warnings: Do not stop taking this medication suddenly without talking to your doctor, as this can cause serious problems. Tell your doctor if you notice unusual urges such as gambling, eating, or other compulsive behaviors, as this medicine can sometimes cause these. It may cause sudden sleepiness, so be careful driving or using machinery. If you have a history of certain mental health conditions, skin cancer, or glaucoma, make sure your doctor knows before starting this medicine.
typical_dosing: Dosing is very individual and your doctor will start you on a low dose and slowly increase it to find what works best for you. A common starting dose is one tablet of carbidopa 25 mg and levodopa 100 mg taken 3 times a day. Extended-release capsules (Rytary) are taken 3 times daily as well. Always take it as prescribed and try to take it at the same times each day for best results.
